The new contracts further expand the company's extensive single asset Cryptocurrency product suite, which includes Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Solana, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche, and Sui futures.

Coinbase Derivatives is planning on expanding 24/7 trading for its listed altcoin futures, including Avalanche, Bitcoin Cash, Cardano, Chainlink, Dogecoin, Hedera, Litecoin, Polkadot, Shiba Inu, Stellar, and SUI.

Releasers define how tokens in the TokenJar are accessed. The simplest version burns UNI in exchange for the collected tokens. Other Releasers could handle cross-chain conversions or alternative value flows.
The proposal of UNIfication has been passed by more than 125 million UNI votes by Uniswap governance, which was well above the expected quorum.

to be an eligible holding under the generic listing standards, the Proposals provide that, for each commodity, or commodity that underlies a commodity-based asset, the commodity may (1) trade on an ISG market; or (2) have futures traded for at least six months on a DCM that is an ISG market or with which an Exchange has a CSSA.
We propose governance create an annual growth budget of 20M UNI, distributed quarterly using a vesting contract starting January 1, 2026, to fund protocol growth and development.

thesis: [uni-new-fact] states CME will launch UNI futures on October 19, pending regulatory review. [uni-new-fact-2] lists CME's existing single-asset crypto suite, and UNI is not in it. [uni-prior-1] lists Coinbase Derivatives' altcoin futures, also without UNI. Inference: this is UNI's first CME listing, and no earlier disclosure of it was found. Inference: a regulated CME contract widens institutional access to UNI exposure and starts the six-month futures clock in [uni-mechanism-3], one route to a generic-standard UNI ETP. No excerpt shows the listing itself changing Uniswap protocol fees or the UNI burn.
economic_relationship: Protocol channel: in [uni-mechanism-1], collected fees can be released by burning UNI, and [uni-mechanism-2] shows governance passed UNIfication. So burn-driven value depends on protocol fee volume, which a CME futures listing does not directly change. Access channel: under [uni-mechanism-3], a commodity can qualify for generic ETP listing after its futures trade for six months on a DCM that is an ISG market or has a CSSA. Explicit assumptions, not supported by any excerpt: CME counts as such a DCM for the listing exchange; UNI does not already qualify by another route; any resulting ETP demand is net spot buying. Futures also add hedging and short capacity, which can push price either way.
disproof: Refuted if CME does not list UNI futures by October 19, or if regulatory review blocks or delays them [uni-new-fact]. Refuted if UNI futures volume and open interest stay negligible in the first 30 days of trading. Refuted if UNI does not outperform a matched large-cap alt basket over the 30 days after listing. The ETF-route inference is refuted if UNI turns out to already meet the generic listing standard by another route. The burn-value link is refuted if protocol-fee UNI burns do not exceed the growth-budget issuance in [uni-adverse-1] over the same period.

sources.excerpt: PORTSMOUTH, N.H., Sept. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bottomline, a global leader in business payments, has launched Global Pay Connect, a next-generation Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform, to help financial institutions extend their payments infrastructure beyond traditional connectivity through API-enabled services and third-party data integration.

Global Pay Connect enables interoperability through Chainlink, connecting banks seamlessly to multiple blockchain networks through a single, network-agnostic integration model via their existing Bottomline connectivity.

frequently described as one of the three largest firms that help institutions use the Swift messaging system, entered a strategic collaboration with the oracle and interoperability platform on September 3
This follows a strategic partnership between Bottomline and Chainlink first announced on September 3, meaning today's update marks the platform itself going live, not a new partnership announcement.

The Chainlink Reserve is designed to support the long-term growth and sustainability of the Chainlink Network by accumulating LINK tokens using offchain revenue from large enterprises that are adopting the Chainlink standard and from onchain service usage.

This enables revenue from both onchain service usage, as well as significant offchain revenue from existing and ongoing enterprise integrations, usage and maintenance, to be programmatically converted to LINK (if not already paid in LINK).
Neither company has disclosed which banks will use the service first or when initial live transactions will settle through it.

thesis: [link-new-fact] (Sept. 17 dateline) states Bottomline launched Global Pay Connect, and [link-new-fact-2] says it connects banks to multiple blockchains through Chainlink. [link-prior-1] shows the Bottomline-Chainlink strategic collaboration was announced September 3, and [link-prior-2] describes the Sept. 17 news as the platform going live, not a new partnership. Inference: the only new substance is that the product is now available. The relationship itself was already public. No excerpt gives fees, volumes or named adopting banks [link-adverse-1].
economic_relationship: [link-mechanism-1]: the Chainlink Reserve accumulates LINK using offchain enterprise revenue and onchain usage. [link-mechanism-2]: that revenue is programmatically converted to LINK. Proposed chain: bank flows over Global Pay Connect use Chainlink services, fees go to Chainlink, the fees are converted to LINK, and the LINK goes into the Reserve. Explicit assumptions NOT supported by any excerpt: Bottomline or its banks pay Chainlink material usage fees; those fees go through Payment Abstraction; volume arrives within a tradable horizon. Because no fees or volumes are disclosed, the size of any LINK demand is unknown.
disproof: Refuted if no named bank goes live or settles a transaction through Global Pay Connect via Chainlink within about 90 days [link-adverse-1]. Refuted if Chainlink Reserve LINK accumulation shows no acceleration after launch. Refuted if LINK does not outperform a matched large-cap alt basket over the 30 days after Sept. 17. The novelty claim is refuted if the Sept. 17 release adds no substantive fact beyond the Sept. 3 partnership, as [link-prior-1] and [link-prior-2] suggest.

sources.excerpt: CHEYENNE, Wyo., September 16, 2026: Payward, the parent company of Kraken, today announced that it intends to deploy onchain perpetual futures markets for US clients, starting with Hyperliquid HIP-3* markets, the protocol’s first builder-deployed permissioned perpetual markets.
Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, would be the HIP-3* deployer: it would create, own and administer the market and clear and settle the contracts.

Hyperliquid Labs is reportedly talking with Kraken parent Payward to bring some of its perpetual futures to US traders through Bitnomial, a US-regulated digital asset exchange and clearinghouse, Bloomberg reported citing people familiar with the matter.

On Hyperliquid, fees are entirely directed to the community (HLP, the assistance fund, and deployers). Spot and HIP-3 perp deployers may choose to keep up to 50% of trading fees generated by their deployed assets.
It converts trading fees to HYPE in a fully automated manner as part of the L1 execution. HYPE in the assistance fund is burned, removing the tokens permanently from the circulating and total supply.
The staking requirement for mainnet will be 500k HYPE. This requirement is expected to decrease over time as the infrastructure matures.
Subject to regulatory approval, onchain perpetual futures will be listed under the rules of Bitnomial Exchange, LLC.

thesis: [hype-new-fact] states Payward announced on 2026-09-16 that it intends to deploy US-client perpetual markets starting with Hyperliquid HIP-3* markets, and [hype-new-fact-2] states Bitnomial would be the HIP-3* deployer. [hype-prior-1] shows a Payward/Bitnomial/Hyperliquid plan was already reported before this, so the new content is the formal confirmation plus structure details (deployer, clearing), not the existence of the plan. Inference: if approved and live, US order flow adds fee-paying volume on Hyperliquid and requires a deployer stake in HYPE. The announcement is an intent. It is not a launch.
economic_relationship: Per [hype-mechanism-1], trading fees go to HLP, the assistance fund and deployers, and HIP-3 deployers may keep up to 50%. Per [hype-mechanism-2], the assistance fund converts fees to HYPE and burns it. Per [hype-mechanism-3], a HIP-3 deployer must stake 500k HYPE, and that requirement is expected to decrease. Explicit assumptions, not supported by any excerpt: (a) the Bitnomial markets generate material volume; (b) Bitnomial's 500k HYPE stake is net new demand, not HYPE already held or staked; (c) Bitnomial does not choose the maximum deployer fee share. No fee schedule, volume estimate or launch date is in the excerpts.
disproof: Refuted if, by 2027-03-31, no Bitnomial-deployed HIP-3* market is live on Hyperliquid mainnet with US allowlisted traders, for example because the approval in [hype-adverse-1] is not granted. Also refuted if onchain data shows the deployer's 500k HYPE stake was moved from existing staked or treasury HYPE, with no open-market purchase. Also refuted if, in the first 90 days after launch, the Bitnomial markets' protocol fees are under 1% of assistance-fund HYPE purchases.

sources.excerpt: Aave V4 launches on Arc, Circle's USDC-native Layer 1. The market deploys a Core Hub with Main and Forex Spokes, listing USDC, EURC, cirBTC, and WETH.

Execution will happen alongside the Arc network launch on September 16th. The ARFC snapshot is taken as the binding vote for this execution, and Aave Labs is coordinating the activation alongside the network launch.
Aave Labs proposes deploying Aave V4 on Arc, the institutional-grade public layer-1 blockchain built by Circle, at or near Arc mainnet launch.
The Liquidity Fee is the fraction of borrower interest captured by the protocol treasury, equivalent to the reserve factor in V3.
The Aave DAO operates a buyback program that uses protocol revenue to acquire AAVE tokens on the open market.

In connection with the deployment, Aave DAO is expected to receive a minimum of $2m per year in protocol revenue from the Aave V4 deployment on Arc, with any shortfalls covered by certain Arc ecosystem participants for the first five years following deployment.

Following the rsETH bridge incident on April 18, 2026, AAVE buybacks have been paused since April 19, 2026. This ARFC formalises the pause and outlines the conditions under which the buyback cadence will be reassessed.

sources.excerpt: Mainnet activation: completed September 22, 2026 at 11:00 AM ET (15:00 UTC). Mainnet validators must be running AvalancheGo v1.15.0

This release schedules the activation of the Helicon network upgrade at 11 AM ET (3 PM UTC) on Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026 on Mainnet. All Mainnet nodes must upgrade before 11 AM ET, September 22nd 2026.
ACP-285 Reduce Minimum Consumption Rate The ACPs in this upgrade go into effect at 11 AM ET (3 PM UTC) on Tuesday, July 28th, 2026 on the Fuji Testnet.

First, lowering the reward-rate floor cuts the rewards given to short-duration stakes. This is projected to reduce the AVAX inflation rate by 0.5 to 1 percentage point per year, reflecting a lower reward rate partially offset by longer average staking durations.

ACP-285 is now ramping in over the 90 days that follow Helicon's activation on September 22, 2026, starting at 10% and settling at 7.5% along a straight line, so protocols and strategies priced on the previous rates can reprice instead of absorbing a discontinuous shock.

Empirical evidence is mixed on whether the wider premium will flip large validators' duration choices. Conversations with node operators and large-position stakers suggest that liquidity preference may dominate even a 2.30 percentage point premium for some cohorts.

The change affects only new staking periods initiated after activation. Validators and delegators with active staking positions at the time of activation continue to receive rewards under the original parameters for the remainder of their existing stake periods.

thesis: [avax-new-fact-2] says Helicon mainnet activation was scheduled for Sept 22, 2026; [avax-new-fact] says it was completed then. [avax-mechanism-2] says ACP-285 lowers the reward floor from 10% to 7.5% over 90 days, and [avax-mechanism-1] projects AVAX inflation will fall 0.5 to 1 pp per year. Inference: new AVAX issuance begins a gradual decline from Sept 22, 2026. Adverse: [avax-prior-1] shows ACP-285 was already scheduled on Fuji for July 28, 2026, so the rule change was public before; the new facts are only the mainnet date and its completion. [avax-adverse-2] says active stakes keep the old parameters, and [avax-adverse-1] calls the duration response uncertain, so any supply effect is slow and depends on the model.
economic_relationship: [avax-mechanism-1]: lowering the reward floor cuts rewards to short-duration stakes and is projected to reduce AVAX inflation by 0.5 to 1 pp per year. [avax-mechanism-2]: the floor ramps from 10% to 7.5% over 90 days. Channel: fewer newly minted AVAX per year means slower supply growth. Assumption (not in excerpts): some share of staking rewards gets sold, so lower issuance reduces sell flow. Assumption (not in excerpts): lower yields don't cause enough unstaking or lost demand to offset this. No fee switch, buyback or burn is sourced here; the only value channel is lower issuance.
disproof: Refuted if (a) P-Chain reward parameters show new stakes started after Sept 22, 2026 still get the 10% minimum consumption rate, with no ramp toward 7.5% as [avax-mechanism-2] describes; or (b) AVAX net issuance annualized over the 90-day ramp is not lower than the trailing pre-activation rate, for example because legacy stakes keep old terms ([avax-adverse-2]) or stakers pick durations that raise emissions ([avax-adverse-1]); or (c) the substantive content of [avax-new-fact] and [avax-new-fact-2] turns out to be identical to [avax-prior-1] apart from the network name and date.

sources.excerpt: This proposal signals the intent of the DAO to introduce dotUSD, Polkadot's native stablecoin, as the protocol's primary stable-value instrument.
Use treasury funds for the initial liquidity in the DOT x dotUSD pool. $2.5M in USDT will be used to mint dotUSD and $2.5M in DOT will be allocated initially to the pool.
pUSD (Polkadot USD over-collateralised debt token) is a new DOT-collateralized stablecoin deployed on Asset Hub. It is an overcollateralized stablecoin backed purely by DOT.
The fundamental operation is straightforward: a user locks DOT, and against that collateral mints dotUSD at a value less than the collateral deposited.

Phase 2 - DOT-collateralized Vault dotUSD The second phase introduces the complete vault system with DOT collateral, oracle integration, the stability pool, liquidation mechanics and the redemption mechanism.

The first phase, which is already built and on chain, releases only the stables buffer mechanism: users may mint dotUSD one-to-one against USDT which can be redeemed for 1 USD, subject to a cap. This requires no oracle, no vaults and no liquidation logic

In Polkadot's case, the relationship is bidirectional: dotUSD's success is tied to DOT's utility, and DOT's economic model increasingly depends upon dotUSD as the instrument through which specific treasury operations will be denominated.

thesis: [dot-new-fact] says Referendum 1944 signals DAO intent to make dotUSD Polkadot's primary stable-value instrument. [dot-new-fact-2] says $2.5M USDT will mint dotUSD and $2.5M of treasury DOT will seed a DOT x dotUSD pool. [dot-mechanism-1] describes users locking DOT to mint dotUSD, but [dot-mechanism-2] puts DOT-collateral vaults in Phase 2, and [dot-adverse-1] says Phase 1 mints dotUSD 1:1 against USDT with no vaults. Inference: passing Ref 1944 locks no DOT as collateral by itself. DOT locking depends on a later Phase 2, and no excerpt gives it a date. [dot-prior-1] shows a DOT-collateralized native stablecoin (pUSD) had already been proposed, so the concept isn't new; the new element is a formal referendum with treasury funding.
economic_relationship: [dot-mechanism-1]: users lock DOT as over-collateral to mint dotUSD, which removes DOT from liquid supply while vaults stay open. [dot-mechanism-2]: that vault system only arrives in Phase 2. [dot-new-fact-2]: $2.5M of treasury DOT gets paired with dotUSD in a pool. Assumption (not in excerpts): Phase 2 ships and borrowers want enough dotUSD to lock a material amount of DOT. Assumption (not in excerpts): pool activity and redemptions add no net DOT sell flow. [dot-adverse-2] says the DOT/dotUSD link runs both ways: a falling DOT price weakens dotUSD's collateral, so the channel is reflexive, not one-way.
disproof: Refuted if Ref 1944 is rejected or times out. Also refuted if, at the review horizon, no Phase-2 DOT-collateral vault is live on-chain and all dotUSD has been minted against USDT as [dot-adverse-1] describes, leaving DOT locked as dotUSD collateral at zero. Also refuted if, after Phase 2 goes live, DOT locked in vaults stays small next to the $2.5M of DOT the treasury seeds into the pool ([dot-new-fact-2]), or if a DOT drawdown triggers vault liquidations or redemptions that sell DOT, the reflexive risk in [dot-adverse-2].
